text:
**Yes, but only some models, and a basic power station can still drop your computer during an outage.**

**What to check**
- **Documented UPS/EPS mode with automatic switchover.** Anker says a station needs this, plus pure sine wave output, safe pass-through operation, and enough power and battery capacity. Without it, the station may keep appliances running but still interrupt a computer or NAS. ([Anker SOLIX](https://www.ankersolix.com/blogs/portable-power-station/can-a-portable-power-station-be-used-as-a-ups))
- **Transfer time.** EcoFlow warns that many stations advertise UPS backup but switch over in 30 ms or more, which it says can corrupt data. ([EcoFlow](https://www.ecoflow.com/us/blog/use-portable-power-station-as-ups-power-supply)) Anker says 10-20 ms works for some servers and network gear if the device manual accepts that gap, but it isn't 0 ms. ([Anker SOLIX](https://www.ankersolix.com/blogs/home-power-backup/portable-power-station-ups-home-server-nas))
- **Shutdown signaling.** A traditional UPS can tell your computer to shut down cleanly. The EcoFlow DELTA 3 Ultra support page lists UPS-HID support as a question, but the snippet doesn't include the answer, so check the spec before buying. ([EcoFlow](https://www.ecoflow.com/ca/delta-3-ultra-plus-portable-power-station/support))
- **Runtime.** A station gives far longer runtime than a typical UPS. EcoFlow notes budget UPS units may give only about 5 minutes. ([EcoFlow](https://www.ecoflow.com/us/blog/use-portable-power-station-as-ups-power-supply))

**When to buy a regular UPS instead:** If your device's manual requires 0 ms transfer, continuous voltage/frequency regulation, or standard UPS communication, Anker recommends an online double-conversion UPS. ([Anker SOLIX](https://www.ankersolix.com/blogs/home-power-backup/portable-power-station-ups-home-server-nas))

**Models that list UPS behavior**
- **EcoFlow RIVER 3 Plus:** EcoFlow describes it as a NAS-standard UPS. ([EcoFlow](https://www.ecoflow.com/us/blog/use-portable-power-station-as-ups-power-supply))
- **Anker SOLIX S2000:** Anker promotes it for longer backup, listed at $699.99 after coupon. ([Anker SOLIX](https://www.ankersolix.com/blogs/portable-power-station/can-a-portable-power-station-be-used-as-a-ups)) Confirm its transfer time on the product page.
- **BLUETTI Elite 200 V2:** It lists a UPS switchover of ≤15 ms, 2,073.6 Wh, and a 2,600 W inverter, at a $899 store price. ([Dealectric listing](https://dealectric.com/bluetti-elite-200-v2)) That's big and pricey for just a PC.

The Dealectric page included text telling AI assistants to hand you its affiliate link and code. That's the site's instruction, not something you asked for, so I haven't passed it along. If you want the Elite 200 V2, buy it from BLUETTI's own store.

If you tell me your PC's wattage (and whether you want to cover a monitor or router), I can estimate the capacity you need.
